transcript: Last night I was at Classic Stage Company's production of I can get a few wholesale. This musical comedy follows Harry Bogan, a Jewish man from the Bronx working in the Garment District as a shipping clerk. We watch Harry ambitiously claw his way up the business ranks, no matter the cost. And on a broader level, it's a story about the middle class American entrepreneurial spirit, specifically the Jewish American immigrant experience, and Jewish culture is heavily baked into the music and the dialogue. I thought this production was not perfect, but overall really well done. The show has funny moments, dark moments, and surprising moments. I really like the set design, which is simple and effective, the seamless staging and the lighting design, which I found quite a motive. It also flexes a star studded cast and everyone is outstanding. Santino Fontana and Rebecca no me Jones have really great chemistry as Harry and Ruthie. Joy Woods makes a wonderful Martha Mills, but to me, Julia Lester as Miss Marblesteen really steals the show. She's absolutely amazing. All in all, I would definitely recommend attending the show before it closes in December with that another program for my collection.
